business_objective: Track temporary checkout and return of original files and close each custody record after the returned file condition is documented.

stakeholder_statements.text: A records requester submits an original-file checkout request and identifies the file and business purpose.
The archive clerk records the original file as available or unavailable for checkout.
The records custodian issues the original file only when availability is recorded and records the recipient.
The return inspector records the file as returned complete or returned damaged and adds a note when it is damaged.
The archive supervisor closes the checkout record only after the return condition is recorded. Copying the file and changing its contents are outside this project.

business_objective: Review traveler-to-room assignments and publish an approved rooming list when bookings and assigned rooms are confirmed.

stakeholder_statements.text: A group coordinator submits a rooming-list release request and identifies the trip, accommodation booking, and traveler-to-room assignments.
The booking agent records each traveler as active or inactive for the trip. The active-booking criteria have not been agreed.
The accommodation liaison records each assigned room as available or unavailable and records any occupancy restriction. The occupancy-restriction categories are not finalized.
The travel operations reviewer records the rooming list as approved or returned and adds a reason when it is returned. The approval criteria are undecided.

The manifest clerk publishes the rooming list only after every traveler is active, every assigned room is available, and release approval is recorded, then sends the outcome to the group coordinator. The delivery channel is undecided. Changing traveler names and collecting accommodation payments are outside this project.

business_objective: Review temporary payment-card control changes and apply authorized, acceptable-risk, approved controls for the intended-use period.

stakeholder_statements.text: An account holder submits a temporary card-control change and identifies the card, current control, requested control, and intended-use period. The allowed control types have not been finalized.
The card authority reviewer records whether the requester is authorized to change the card control. The authority-check criteria have not been agreed.
The fraud risk reviewer records the requested change as acceptable, heightened risk, or prohibited. The risk criteria are undecided.
The operations approver records the change as approved or returned and adds a reason when it is returned.

The card controls clerk applies the requested control only after requester authority, a non-prohibited risk outcome, and approval are recorded, then sends the outcome to the account holder. The delivery channel is undecided. Processing card transactions and issuing replacement cards are outside this project.

business_objective: Review removal of temporary site signage and clear signs for removal after safety-information, access-route, and approval checks.

stakeholder_statements.text: A site coordinator submits a temporary-signage removal request and identifies the sign, location, and removal reason.
The safety inspector records whether replacement safety information remains available after removal. The safety-information criteria have not been agreed.
The access route reviewer records the removal impact as none, manageable, or blocking. The impact-assessment criteria are undecided.
The project engineer records the request as approved or returned and adds a reason when it is returned. The approval criteria are not finalized.

The site records clerk marks the sign cleared for removal only after replacement safety information, a non-blocking access-route impact, and approval are recorded, then sends the outcome to the site coordinator. The delivery channel is undecided. Physically removing signs and designing replacement signs are outside this project.

business_objective: Review proposed secondary use of archived research recordings while preserving an unresolved rule about whether broad consent permits a new research purpose.

stakeholder_statements.text: A research archivist submits a secondary-use review and identifies the originating study, recording set, and proposed secondary purpose.
The consent analyst records the consent wording associated with the recording set. The analyst says broad research consent permits internal secondary use for a new research purpose.
The participant rights reviewer records a privacy assessment. The reviewer says fresh participant consent is required for every new research purpose.
The de-identification reviewer records the recording set as de-identified or not de-identified and records any restrictions. The criteria for adequate de-identification have not been agreed.

The research governance chair records the review as approved or declined and records a decision rationale after the consent wording, privacy assessment, and de-identification outcome are present. Nobody has decided which consent rule controls, who resolves the disagreement, what evidence proves fresh consent, which secondary-purpose categories qualify for review, or the maximum review time. Conducting the secondary analysis and contacting participants are outside this project; the meeting also wandered into complaints about the recorder cabinet.
